title: Your phone and your future: earn, learn and stay safe

say: Your phone and your future: earn, learn and stay safe.
This is the video for Module 4 of Smartphone and Digital Awareness: digital literacy and your future.
A smartphone does not make money by itself. It helps you show what you sell, reach customers, take orders and receive payment.

say: For example, Adunni in Ibadan makes plantain chips. She posts daylight photos with the price and how to order, and sells about 40 packs a week.
Each pack sells for about 1,000 naira.
Ingredients and packaging cost about 600 naira per pack.
So she makes 400 naira on each pack. That is 16,000 naira a week, and 64,000 naira over 4 weeks.
After about 5,000 naira for data, airtime and delivery, she earns about 59,000 naira a month. She records every sale, so she knows the real figure.
Show your product clearly, with the price.

say: Genuine work pays you. Schemes take your money. Be suspicious if you must pay to join, if you earn by recruiting others, or if it promises to double your money.
Watch out when you are paid small amounts for easy tasks, then asked to deposit more to unlock earnings. If you are caught, stop paying, keep screenshots, and call your bank on its official number.

panel.heading: Signs of a scheme, not a job
items: You must pay to join or buy a package
You earn by recruiting others who pay
Promises to double your money
Small pay first, then deposit to unlock
Pressure to act now, no real address

say: Your NIN and BVN are keys to your identity and money. Never post photos of your NIN slip, ID card, passport or ATM card.
For example, Chiamaka in Enugu searches her own name before a job application. She deletes an old angry post, and asks a friend to remove a photo of her ID card.

panel.heading: What to keep off the internet
left: NIN slip, ID card or passport

say: Then she uses the same name and a clear photo on WhatsApp and LinkedIn, with an honest one-line bio.

say: The Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 gives you rights over your personal data, enforced by the NDPC. For example, Ladi in Lafia keeps getting marketing calls. She emails the company, asks what data they hold, and asks them to stop marketing to her.

panel.heading: Using your data rights
items: Write to the company, in writing
Keep copies, dates and screenshots
Wait for a reply
Escalate to the right regulator

say: To remember. Confirm payment in your own app. Never pay to join a money scheme. Study at a fixed time.
Keep ID documents off the internet, and use your rights in writing.
Finally, write a 30-day plan with three SMART goals: safety, organisation and growth.
